title.narrative: Support to home based care initiatives

description.narrative:
FRACODEP implements an HIV and AIDS home based care (HBC) project for people living with HIV and AIDS (PLWHA) in the three parishes; St. Paul, Rang’ala and Nyango’oma. This project focus on HIV prevention and home based care. It provides friendly Voluntary Counselling and Testing (VCT) services, capacity building for staff, PLWHA and community vounteers. Community mobilisation and sensitisation, production and dissemination of IEC materials and networking and collaboration are other key activities. Voluntary Counselling and Testing has a crucial role to play as the entry point to HIV prevention and home care. Availability and accessibility to VCTs enables early diagnosis and timely treatment while those who test positive will receive care and support and live positively, those who test negative are encouraged to retain their HIV negative status. Overly, the project reaches over 10,000 people including men, women and children infected with and affected by HIV and AIDS Integrating VCT in HBC provides an opportunity for provision of holistic and meaningful benefits to PLWHA and OVCs. Nutrition plays key role in health of PLWHA especially those on treatment to ensure drug adherence. More people have appreciated and have adopted good practice in nutrition through the linkage between HBC and VCT for their improved health. Clients on the programme are getting better and living positively.
There is value addition to the project delivery in terms for knowledge of HIV status, behaviour change, improved physical status of clients, increased acceptance of HIV status, reduced stigma at individual, family and community level, disclosure, and positive living. Additionally, infected people seek early treatment, and awareness of what to do such as adopting good practices such as drug adherence, use of nutritious foods and sharing of personal experiences. To ensure change occurs, qualified and committed staff including project officers VCT counsellors, Clinical Officer, nutritionist and field officer are on board. National and international standards’ required in service delivery are complied with. The local community is a collaborator to the project.
